 Between now and the break, there's only one match at the bewitched Dall'Ara. They're the team that has worsened the most since '25-'26: 8 points less. Now they need a Bologna side that can travel. Three away games to banish the fear.
 It began with Bologna finishing second to last on the eve of their trip to Lecce this October. To avoid ending it...
 di MARCELLO GIORDANO October 22, 2026 Raffaele Palladino, 42 years old (Alive)
 Facebook X WhatsApp Print It began with Bologna second to last on the eve of their trip to Lecce this October. To avoid ending the season in the red, a change of pace is needed. And who knows, perhaps a team with relegation-worthy numbers and a deep home crisis at the Dall'Ara (2 wins, 11 defeats, and 5 draws in their last 18 matches since November 9, 2025) will find themselves blessing a schedule that presents them with two consecutive away games and three trips in the next four matchdays separating them from the next break, also considering the match at the Tardini against Parma on November 7. After all, despite the darkness of this start to the season, the rossoblù's only win has come on the road, at Lecce, and with it, three of the five points earned in the standings so far. These difficulties have also affected their away form, considering the defeats in Bergamo and Napoli. 
 From November to May, Bologna recorded 8 wins, 3 defeats, and 2 draws away from the Dall'Ara, averaging 2 points per game (26 points in 13 games), a step away from Europe. Indeed, they were in the running for the Conference with Palladino's Atalanta until the end. Even adding the wins and two defeats from this early season, the record remains more than good (29 points in 16 games, 1,8 points per game), with a projected 69 points for the season. 
 That the primary problem is home form is undeniable, and Cagliari's latest 4-0 defeat at Monza gives the Rossoblu some confidence. "We're back to earth," the Sardinians said after the match. Bologna has the tough task of proving whether that's true or whether the latest defeat was a blip due to a lack of concentration. Indeed, even after the latest defeat, Cagliari remains the second most improved team in Serie A: Pisacane's team has 5 more points than a year ago (13 vs. 8), only Gattuso's Lazio (+11, 19 vs. 8) has done better in this particular performance ranking. 
 And Bologna? They're the team that has worsened the most, the one that has lost the most points compared to last season, from 13 a year ago to five now: -8, the thermometer says. They'll be playing in Cagliari on matchday eight: and it was on matchday eight, two years ago, that Italiano's first Bologna, drawing 2-2 in Genoa with goals from Orsolini and Odgaard, slipped to thirteenth place. But they found their true form (with Odgaard as attacking midfielder), then soared to fourth place with a month to go in the championship, winning the Coppa Italia and climbing to first place in the table in November 2025, when the home crisis began. Today, Bologna is fifteenth, one point above the relegation zone. They need points and signs of continuity from the first half against Inter; the Rossoblu need to believe that Palladino can find his Bologna in October.
